behaviour_changes.3_visible_set_aggregates: All nine aggregates are now visible-set aggregates. A caller that could previously read another tenant's whole-subgraph counts now reads only its visible part. This is the point of the PR.
behaviour_changes.4_agent_and_orphan_rows_excluded: ownership rows with node_type = 'agent', and rows whose node_id names no surviving row, now drop out of node_counts, temporal_bins, degrees and clustering_coefficients - for EVERY principal, including the owner. `agents` carries no tenancy columns so no predicate can decide it, and ownership has no FK to the tables it points at. This NARROWS THE OWNER'S OWN ANSWERS, which no acceptance line asks for; it is fail-closed per D1 (cannot classify is not public) rather than a fail-closed regression of the §R2 shape, because the rows are excluded rather than erroring. Asserted for both principals by owner_sees_the_whole_subgraph_and_a_stranger_only_its_public_part so the exclusion stays visible.
behaviour_changes.5_clustering_and_conflict_errors_now_500: Both statements used to end .unwrap_or_default(), rendering a query failure as an empty distribution. They now propagate.
behaviour_changes.6_clustering_stats_was_always_zero: A REAL PRE-EXISTING BUG, fixed here and observable only because of change 5. `2.0` and `1.0` are numeric literals in Postgres, so COALESCE(2.0 * tri_count / (deg * (deg - 1.0)), 0.0) had type numeric, which sqlx cannot decode into f64. EVERY request over a subgraph containing an actual triangle returned Err, and .unwrap_or_default() turned it into {mean: 0, variance: 0, eligible_nodes: 0}. The endpoint has reported zero clustering for exactly the graphs the statistic was written to describe since it existed. Fixed with ::double precision casts.
behaviour_changes.7_counts_and_moments_no_longer_agree: A CONSEQUENCE of fixing critic finding M3, stated so it is not read as a bug. Because the four moment blocks now have their COUNT component noised while their mean/variance/max stay exact, a default-epsilon response can carry degree_stats.total_nodes = 0 beside a non-zero mean and max_degree, or conflict_stats.entries = 3 beside mean = 0.0. The count and the moments in one block are no longer mutually consistent. This is the mechanism behaving correctly - noising a count down to zero is part of what partially mitigates F-structural-support-exact for the scalar fields - and `noise_applied: true` already tells a client not to read the numbers as exact. See F-structural-moments-exact.

scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.note: PR-08 adds a refusal the plan does not ask for. Recorded as a deliberate scope addition rather than slipped in, because a silent deviation is the failure mode this ledger exists to prevent.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.what: MAX_UNPRIVILEGED_EPSILON = 1.0 in routes/structural.rs, and noise_engages became `epsilon.is_finite() && epsilon > 0.0 && epsilon <= MAX_UNPRIVILEGED_EPSILON`. The default IS the ceiling (default_epsilon() returns the constant, pinned by the_default_is_the_ceiling): a caller may buy more privacy, never less.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.why: The gate closed epsilon = 0, -1, NaN and inf and shipped the fourth member of the same class. 1e300 is finite and positive, so it passed the gate UNSCOPED, while b = 1/epsilon = 1e-300 made the noise term round away and the count come back exact - a claims:read caller obtained the exact counts the claims:admin gate exists to withhold, with "noise_applied": true in the body. The plan's literal acceptance line (epsilon=0.0 -> 403) was still satisfied, which is why the first pass and the verifier both let it stand; its PURPOSE (exact counts are an administrative capability) was defeated by one query-string character.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.why_1_0_and_not_10: A ceiling in the conventional DP range would have closed almost nothing. At epsilon=10, b=0.1 and P(|noise| > 0.5) = e^-5 = 0.0067, so 99.3% of single draws are already exact and the mode over a handful of requests is the exact count. At 1.0, b=1.0 and P(|noise| > 0.5) = e^-0.5 = 0.61.
scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling.residual: This closes the SINGLE-REQUEST exact read only. There is still no privacy budget - see open finding F-structural-no-privacy-budget.

critic_findings_2026_09_02.B1_rand_simple_returns_0_to_2_and_NaN_is: FIXED. THE BLOCKER, and PR-08's own default flip is what made it live. routes/structural.rs::rand_simple was documented `[0, 1)` and returned `[0, 2)`: `>> 16` of a u32 lies in [0, 65536) and it divided by 32768 - the divisor was wrong by a factor of two. maybe_add_noise then computed u = r - 0.5 in [-0.5, 1.5), and for every u > 0.5 the term (1 - 2|u|) was NEGATIVE, ln of it NaN, and (value + NaN).round().max(0.0) returned 0, because Rust's f64::max returns the non-NaN operand. Same launder-an-error-into-a-benign-answer shape this PR removed from clustering_coefficients's .unwrap_or_default(), one function away. MEASURED over 1,000,000 seeds with the two functions compiled verbatim: 500,001 returned 0 instead of 42 (50.00%) and 15 hit the |u| == 0.5 boundary where ln(0) = -inf saturates the cast to i64::MAX. Before PR-08 the path was dead (epsilon defaulted to 0.0, apply_noise false); flipping the default to 1.0 put every caller on it, so the endpoint would have reported roughly half of an owner's counts as 0 - reading as `this owner has nothing`, not as garbage. FIX: rand_simple is DELETED and maybe_add_noise draws from `rand` (already a non-optional dependency of epigraph-api - oauth/authorize.rs, spans.rs), whose Rng::gen::<f64>() is uniform on [0, 1) by contract. That also closes the separate defect that rand_simple reseeded an LCG from SystemTime::now().subsec_nanos() on EVERY call, making draws within one request correlated and predictable from the request time. An explicit `arg > 0.0` guard plus an is_finite check mean no NaN or infinity can reach .max(0.0) again. ThreadRng is !Send, so the generator is constructed and dropped inside the synchronous maybe_add_noise and never held across an .await.
critic_findings_2026_09_02.B1_why_no_test_saw_it: maybe_add_noise_never_negative asserted `noisy >= 0` over 100 draws - which the broken code SATISFIED, because 0 was its failure output. The new acceptance test asserted only `noise_applied == true` and never inspected a count. REPLACED by maybe_add_noise_is_centred_on_the_true_value_and_almost_never_zeroes_it: 2000 draws at epsilon=1 over a true count of 100, asserting the median is within 2 of the true value, that fewer than 1% of draws are zero, and that none saturates i64::MAX. Complemented by no_draw_in_the_unit_interval_produces_a_non_finite_noise_term, a deterministic 10,001-point sweep of the whole draw range including both endpoints.
critic_findings_2026_09_02.B1_falsification: The new assertions were replayed against the OLD rand_simple, compiled verbatim standalone, to prove they are falsifying rather than vacuous. Result over 2000 draws at epsilon=1, true count 100: zeros = 1045/2000 against a threshold of 20, so the zero-rate assertion FAILS on the old code; median = 0 against a required [98, 102], so the centredness assertion FAILS on the old code. In the same run the assertion they REPLACE, `all samples >= 0`, PASSES on the old code - which is the vacuity finding demonstrated rather than argued.
critic_findings_2026_09_02.M2_large_epsilon_bypasses_the_claims_adm: FIXED. See scope_addition_epsilon_ceiling. The critic raised this twice, once as major and once as minor recommending it be deferred to a follow-up; taken as major, because the three closed cases and this open one are one class and closing three is not a partial fix.
critic_findings_2026_09_02.M3_moment_count_fields_exact_at_every_ep: FIXED. degree_stats.total_nodes, belief_stats.claims_with_belief, clustering_stats.eligible_nodes and conflict_stats.entries were exact at every epsilon and returned to any claims:read caller in the same response whose five other count fields were gated. total_nodes is the row count of StructuralRepository::degrees - the SAME quantity as the sum of the nominally-noised node_counts - so the gate withheld nothing. FIX: a single noise_all_counts(&mut response, apply, epsilon) applied after the response is assembled, covering all nine count-shaped fields. Noising at each construction site is what allowed four to be missed. The means, variances and maxima are deliberately untouched (F-structural-moments-exact). Covered by noise_all_counts_covers_every_count_and_no_moment (deterministic at epsilon=1e-6, spurious-failure probability ~5e-7 per field), its no-op control, and the HTTP test the_moment_count_fields_are_noised_for_a_caller_without_claims_admin (epsilon=0.001 vs an admin epsilon=0 reference, joint spurious-failure probability ~6e-14, with a non-vacuity check that the exact values are non-zero).

The #[cfg(not(feature = "db"))] stub hardcoded noise_applied: false even when noise_engages(params.epsilon) was true, the only field on which the two builds disagreed. It now mirrors the db handler. noise_all_counts is deliberately NOT called there: every count is a structural zero, and noising them would make the two builds disagree about the NUMBERS, which is worse than the flag mismatch.
minor_and_nit_fixed.viewer_extractor_401_backstop_doc_was_fa: FIXED AS A DOC. The doc is corrected rather than the extractors reordered: viewer_route_table_lint.rs reads handler signature shape, and re-baselining a lint in the same change that fixes a blocker would hide one behind the other.
minor_and_nit_fixed.edge_counts_double_counts: FIXED AS A DOC. `JOIN ownership o ON (e.source_id = o.node_id OR e.target_id = o.node_id)` counts an edge once per OWNED ENDPOINT, so a both-endpoints-owned edge counts twice. Pre-existing and carried over verbatim, but PR-08 is the first thing to pin it as expected output (SUPPORTS == 4 for two seeded edges), so edge_counts's doc now states it. Its Laplace sensitivity is therefore 2, not the 1 maybe_add_noise assumes - open finding F-edge-count-double-counts.
minor_and_nit_fixed.module_docs_restated_as_a_rule: The module doc said `The Laplace mechanism covers FIVE of the nine outputs` and listed four blocks as exact at any epsilon. Both statements are now false, and a false doc comment is what hid B1 for a full implement-verify cycle. Restated as a RULE - every count-shaped field is noised; means, variances and maxima are not - so it cannot drift back into a stale count.

behaviour_changes.9_suggest_alternative_sets_filters_its_e: s1, s2 and contr all carry a predicate now - edges IS in migration 062's tier_a. behaviour_changes.10_submit_ds_evidence_refuses_outright_o: REACHABLE TODAY, independently of PR-12, and the only such change besides #6. The per-id belief read went from `fetch_one` to `fetch_optional(..)?.ok_or_else(|| invalid_request("claim {id} not found"))`, so (a) a NONEXISTENT claim_id now yields invalid_request where it previously yielded RowNotFound -> internal_error, and (b) an INVISIBLE claim is refused identically, which is plan 8.5's indistinguishability property. Unlike the other three per-id oracles PR-09 hardened - ds_auto, link_epistemic, workflows, which all DEGRADE (no prior / skip the recompute / skip the cascade child) - this one aborts the call, so it DOES decide the write half for this tool: a viewer that cannot read a claim cannot submit evidence against it. Correct under D3 (you may not assert about what you may not read), but a decision rather than a side effect, which is why D-PR16-per-id-claim-oracles-write-half is scoped to the other three.
behaviour_changes.11_two_uuid_extractors_are_deliberately_: epigraph-api's `payload_uuids` is a SUPERSET of the SQL's regexp_matches, not an exact mirror. Postgres returns non-overlapping matches (it resumes after the end of each); the Rust scanner slides over every byte offset and collects overlapping windows. So the in-memory half can only drop MORE events than the persisted half - fail-closed. The property to preserve is `rust superset-of sql`, NOT `rust == sql`: narrowing Rust to match Postgres would make the in-memory half the more permissive of the two, which is the direction that leaks. Stated at `payload_uuids` so nobody later 'fixes' the asymmetry.

critic_findings_2026_09_03.B1_event_list_was_default_open_for_every: FIXED, and it was a real blocker. The filter keyed on payload->>'claim_id' while the live emitters do not use that key: routes/conflicts.rs writes conflict.resolved with claim_a_id/claim_b_id/winner_id, routes/gaps.rs writes challenge_id, and both MCP publish_event and POST /api/v1/events accept arbitrary payloads - so any key allowlist is a rule the next emitter escapes. The rule is now 'an event is returned unless some uuid appearing ANYWHERE in its payload names a claims row this viewer cannot read', implemented as regexp_matches(payload::text, '<uuid>', 'g') over the whole serialised document (nested objects, arrays, keys and uuids inside free text all included). Over-collection is safe by construction: a token naming no claims row cannot suppress anything, because the inner EXISTS requires the row first. Both doc blocks were rewritten to describe the property the SQL has. The regex guard the previous revision needed (Postgres does not short-circuit AND, so a sibling-conjunct guard would not stop 'not-a-uuid'::uuid raising 22P02) is no longer needed and its absence is explained: regexp_matches yields only substrings that already matched.

behaviour_changes.1_get_api_v1_webhooks_returns_fewer_rows: Previously every active subscription in the process, to any authenticated principal, with NO webhooks scope required (a claims:read-only token could read the instance's whole delivery topology). Now the caller's own only. Operator tooling that enumerated all subscriptions through this endpoint STOPS WORKING. Deliberate; there is no admin-wide variant and adding one is a new route + allowlist entry + scope, not a fall-through. No secret was ever exposed (#[serde(skip_serializing)] on both secret and the owner field) - the leak was URL/topology inventory.
behaviour_changes.2_get_api_v1_webhooks_id_answers_403_for: Was an IDOR. 403 rather than 404 so that the answer to 'you do not own this' is identical to delete_webhook's, which webhooks_auth_test.rs::delete_webhook_by_different_caller_returns_403 pins. The existence disclosure traded away is bounded: the id is an unguessable v4 uuid and the caller is already authenticated.
behaviour_changes.3_fan_out_delivers_fewer_events_and_the_: An existing external subscriber silently receives fewer deliveries. This is the fix, but it is a live integration contract and the failure mode is silence, not an error, so every suppression emits a warn/error on the `webhook.delivery.suppressed` tracing target with a `reason` field (no_agent_id | viewer_resolve_failed | payload_names_invisible_claim | visibility_probe_failed | no_db_feature). A database outage now STOPS webhook delivery rather than broadcasting every tenant's claims - the intended trade, stated on the function. CAVEAT, stated rather than implied: NO TEST ASSERTS THE LOG LINE FIRES. The `webhook.delivery.suppressed` target is instrumentation, not a control, and it is unverified instrumentation - the crate has no `tracing-test` harness and PR-10 did not add one. An operator whose only signal that tenancy suppressed a delivery is a log line nobody proved emits should read this as 'best effort', not as a guarantee. Adding the harness is a reasonable follow-up; claiming the observability without it would be the asserted-but-false shape this series exists to avoid.
behaviour_changes.4_post_api_v1_webhooks_becomes_db_depend: register_webhook was pure in-memory and could not fail on I/O. It now has a 500 path, including the agent_id FK violation raised when a token names an agent that no longer exists. It also 401s on a token carrying no agent_id, which it previously accepted (storing client_id as the owner).
behaviour_changes.5_admin_stats_webhook_count_semantics:
GET /api/v1/admin/stats computes WebhookStats { webhook_count } from state.webhook_store.len() (routes/admin.rs::system_stats), UNCHANGED as code. Its MEANING changed, and this PR is what changed it: it used to count subscriptions registered in this process since boot; with boot hydration it now counts the cardinality of webhook_subscriptions ACROSS EVERY TENANT, and it survives a restart.

This matters more than a stats field normally would, because `system_stats` takes NO auth extractor and NO check_scopes call - only `State(state)` - and is registered on the `protected` router in both the db and no-db chains, so any authenticated principal with any scope reads it. It discloses a COUNT, never a url, a secret or an owner. But it is also a counterexample to the invariant repos/webhook.rs::list_active's doc originally asserted (`every path out of that store to an HTTP response is ownership-filtered by the handler`), and a written justification whose named invariant the same commit falsifies is worse than the leak. That doc is corrected in the land phase to say what is true - CONTENT-serialising paths are ownership-filtered, system_stats discloses cardinality only - and the scope gate is left to F-PR10-admin-stats-unscoped rather than bolted on here: SystemStats is a fourteen-field aggregate and two of its tests assert on webhook_count.

Its own test (admin.rs::test_system_stats_reflects_webhook_store) is inside a `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "db")))]` module that, as MEASURED in gate.no_db_all_targets_EXTRA_NOT_PART_OF_THE_GATE, does not compile in any configuration - so nothing would have caught a regression here either way. That is now a measurement rather than the inference it was.
behaviour_changes.6_subscriptions_survive_a_restart:
The first deploy after this lands resurrects nothing (the table starts empty); every subsequent one preserves state. This was previously recorded as pure upside. IT HAS TWO COSTS, and both rest on a SINGLE-INSTANCE ASSUMPTION that the code makes nowhere and documented nowhere until now.
  (a) REVOCATION IS NOT PROCESS-WIDE. delete_webhook removes the row and its own process's cache entry. Any other api instance that hydrated that row at boot keeps subscriptions_matching returning it and keeps POSTing HMAC-signed payloads to an endpoint the owner revoked, until that instance restarts. Before PR-10 this could not happen: a subscription existed only in the process that registered it, so `store.remove` in that process was complete revocation.
  (b) DUPLICATE DELIVERY. Before PR-10 one event produced one delivery, because only the registering process held the subscription. After hydration every instance holds every subscription, so a subscriber receives N copies per event on an N-instance deployment.
Neither fires on a single instance, which is what this host runs. Filed as F-PR10-webhook-store-no-cross-process-invalidation and D-PR-webhook-store-invalidation rather than fixed: a read-through cache with TTL or an event-bus invalidation channel is a mechanism, not a tenancy filter, and adding one inside a security PR is the kind of scope growth this series avoids. NOTE the related asymmetry recorded under open_findings: a delete routed to a process that never saw the row 404s from the cache BEFORE the repo call, so on a multi-instance deployment the row can be unreachable. delete_webhook was NOT reordered to delete-then-404, because deriving 404 from rows_affected is a behaviour change on a single instance for a multi-instance-only benefit; instead the discarded rows_affected is now bound and a `rows == 0` divergence is logged at warn.
behaviour_changes.7_delete_webhook_no_longer_stalls_the_we: LAND-PHASE FIX to code this PR wrote. The handler took `state.webhook_store.write().await`, then awaited the repo delete WHILE STILL HOLDING THE GUARD, and only then called `store.remove(&id)`. tokio's RwLock is fair, so a pending writer blocks new readers: for the whole duration of the DB round trip, deliver_event's per-event read lock, list_webhooks, get_webhook and register_webhook all blocked. A hung Postgres would therefore have stalled the very fan-out this PR exists to make correct - and on this host a wedged Postgres is not hypothetical (pgBackRest ENOSPC crash-looped prod for hours; the static-IP boot race recurs on every reboot). This was an oversight against the file's OWN discipline, not a considered trade: register_webhook deliberately persists BEFORE taking the write lock, and start_webhook_dispatcher's doc explicitly claims the store lock is not held across an await. Clippy cannot see it (`await_holding_lock` fires only on std::sync::MutexGuard). Now: the owner's agent_id is copied out under a READ guard which is dropped at the end of the block, the ownership decision runs on the copy, the DB delete runs with NO guard held, and the write guard is taken solely for `store.remove(&id)`. The observable 401/403/404/204 ordering is unchanged, which webhooks_auth_test.rs (5/5) and webhook_tenancy.rs (10/10) both still pass on.
behaviour_changes.8_the_two_new_500_bodies_no_longer_echo_: register_webhook and delete_webhook build ApiError::InternalError, and errors.rs's IntoResponse serialises `message` straight into the JSON body. Both were `format!("...: {e}")`, which would hand an API client Postgres constraint names, relation names and driver text (e.g. `violates foreign key constraint "webhook_subscriptions_agent_id_fkey"`). register_webhook could not fail on I/O at all before PR-10, so this was a brand-new disclosure surface introduced by this PR rather than an inherited one. The bodies are now fixed strings; the `tracing::error!` one line above already carries the full error for the operator. No test asserted on the old body text (grepped).

PostgreSQL rejects it outright: 'ERROR: transition tables cannot be specified for triggers with column lists'. A column list and a transition table are mutually exclusive, so the migration would have ABORTED on the last statement of the file. Found by executing it. Replaced with `AFTER UPDATE ... REFERENCING OLD TABLE AS prev NEW TABLE AS changed` plus an OLD/NEW comparison as the function's FIRST statement, ahead of the epigraph_definer_bypass() assertion — which restores the intended firing condition and is strictly stricter (a column list fires on a write of the same value; this fires only on a real change). decisions.the_shim_MATERIALIZES_rather_than_refusi: An earlier revision RAISED when the owner had no personal group. That is the wrong trade and 26 test failures made it visible: refusing leaves the claim PUBLIC when the caller asked for private — failing OPEN dressed up as strictness. Minting the agent's own personal group is not a fallback to some other principal's group; it is the same idempotent act ensure_personal_group performs on the OAuth path, yielding a real group whose only live member is the owner. THE GUARD NEEDED A SECOND ESCAPE HATCH, AND A RED TEST FOUND IT. open_findings.detail: The Laplace mechanism is applied per request with no accounting. open_findings.what: The means, variances and maxima of the four moment blocks are exact at every epsilon

PR-08 fixed the COUNT components of these blocks (see critic finding M3), which was an authorization bypass because degree_stats.total_nodes is the same quantity as the sum of the noised node_counts. Bounded: these are all visible-set quantities, so this is a mechanism gap, not a tenancy leak.

open_findings.detail: The needle is `if let Some(axum::Extension(ref auth)) = auth_ctx`. agents.rs::create_agent uses the same idiom in two forms the needle misses: `= &auth_ctx` (trailing &) and `Some(axum::Extension(auth))` (no ref). The ratchet is therefore monotone only against one transcription. Separately, the register's rationale ('harmless only because a ViewerExtractor earlier in the same signature 401s first') does not hold for create_agent, which has no ViewerExtractor and no other auth extractor - nothing in that handler 401s and the agents:write scope is simply unchecked when AuthContext is absent. NOT FIXED IN PR-07: re-baselining that ratchet in the same PR that re-baselines the content-read register would have meant two simultaneous redefinitions, and the second would have hidden the first.
open_findings.assigned: PR-16, which owns the write-path fail-opens the ratchet tracks

open_findings.what: atom_count is derived from an `atoms` CTE filtered only on claim_neighborhood_membership, not on claims
open_findings.detail: The CTE carries /* {VISIBILITY:m} */ only; the returned atom_count therefore tells a stranger how many atoms a compound decomposes into, including atoms whose claims rows it cannot read. No invisible content escapes - the final SELECT filters the compound's own claims row. Inert today because claim_neighborhood_membership.visibility defaults to 'public'. Reportable because MassFunctionRepository::count_for_claim's doc, added by this same PR, spends a paragraph forbidding exactly this shape ('a bare COUNT(*) here would be a cardinality oracle'), and applying that standard in one file and not two files away is an inconsistency worth recording.

open_findings.where: crates/epigraph-api/src/routes/ (97 ViewerExtractor handlers, 62 of which reference `viewer` exactly once)
open_findings.what: No mechanical check distinguishes a handler that spends its Viewer on the content read from one that spends it on an unrelated scalar
open_findings.detail: All 97 handlers reference `viewer` at least once, so there are no literally-unused Viewers; the live defect class is SINGLE-SPEND. Both hypothesis_status (B1) and belief_at_time (M5) were single-spend handlers, and both were found by opening the file rather than by any scan. The adversarial review hand-read roughly a dozen of the 62; the remaining ~50 are unreviewed by any mechanism. The widened viewer_route_table_lint now catches the subset whose second read is an inline tier_a projection - which is what caught the belief_at_time shape - but a handler whose leak is in a repo function it calls with the wrong argument is still invisible.

open_findings.what: No test asserts that a scoped caller's server-derived theme centroid excludes claims it cannot see
open_findings.detail: The statement carries /* {VISIBILITY:c} */ on the averaged SELECT, so the predicate is present and visibility_lint.rs now enforces that it stays. But create_theme_with_centroid_averages_the_claims_when_no_centroid_is_sent uses a claims:admin token over an all-public fixture, so the tenancy half is unasserted. See the crud.rs_create_theme_with_centroid entry in PR-07's scope_substitution.
open_findings.assigned: PR-12 or PR-16, whichever first makes a non-admin caller reach this path

open_findings.what: A spliced statement binds viewer.group_bind().unwrap_or(&[]) unconditionally, which is a Postgres bind-arity error for a Bypass viewer
open_findings.detail: Viewer::render_predicate emits a single space for a Bypass shape, so the rendered statement references no $N while the bind is still supplied -> 'bind message supplies N parameters, but prepared statement requires M'. Fail-CLOSED and unreachable today (this path's viewer never comes from a MaintenanceLease). PR-09 converted all NINE sites it introduced or touched to the guarded `if let Some(g) = viewer.group_bind()` form used by ~165 existing sites, and left this pre-existing one alone rather than widening its diff. A Viewer::bind_groups(q) helper that makes the correct thing the only thing would close the class.

open_findings.what: The --allow-unauthenticated-http listener now reads with the MCP server agent's group set, which is plausibly the largest group in the corpus after PR-12
open_findings.detail: Correctly labelled a widening in auth.rs, viewer.rs and server.rs, and genuinely mitigated today: that listener already injects every scope in SCOPE_MAP, so its holder has full write authority regardless, and migration 062 makes every row public. The forward-looking half is the reportable part - the MCP server agent authors every claim ingested over stdio, so under PR-12's ownership backfill its personal group is plausibly the single largest group in the corpus, and it is handed in one step to whoever holds one shared Caddy bearer token in front of a unix socket. 'Operators who do not want that should not run --allow-unauthenticated-http' is a fair position but it is a DIFFERENT bargain from the one the flag advertised. Options: resolve a dedicated zero-membership principal for that listener (public-only reads, fail-closed, flag keeps its old meaning), or refuse content-reading tools on it outright. Either way it belongs in docs/deploy.md, not only in a doc comment.

open_findings.what: A transient database failure at startup permanently disables every content tool on the --allow-unauthenticated-http listener for the life of the process
open_findings.detail: On error the code logs and stores None, which request_viewer turns into a hard refusal until restart. Before PR-09 the same listener resolved lazily per request and would start working again once the database recovered. The fail-closed choice is right; the once-only caching is the problem. Environment-specific weight: reference_postgres_static_ip_boot_race means Postgres losing its address on reboot is a recurring event here, so a co-scheduled MCP restart can land in exactly this window, and the symptom ('token carries no agent principal' from every tool) does not point at a boot-time DB blip. Fix: hold the id behind an Arc<OnceCell<Uuid>> that request_viewer can lazily re-resolve when it is None, keeping the boot attempt as a warm-up plus the loud error log.

open_findings.what: PR-09 changes four HTTP handlers and adds an HTTP-level test for two of them
open_findings.detail: COVERED: routes/events.rs::list_events (list_events_http_hides_a_private_claim_from_both_the_table_and_the_ring_buffer, killed by mutation M4) and routes/cross_source.rs::list_candidates (list_candidates_http_renders_the_excerpt_of_a_superseded_claim, killed by mutation M5). NOT COVERED at HTTP level: routes/events.rs::graph_snapshot and routes/cross_source.rs::get_cross_source_matches's new scoped 404. Both are covered at the repo layer - graph_snapshot replays the SAME EventRepository::list the covered case exercises, and the 404's underlying reads are covered by tenant_isolation_mcp.rs::find_cross_source_matches_hides_a_corroborates_edge_to_a_private_claim - and both are inert until PR-12 writes the first 'group' row. Recorded rather than asserted, which is the standard PR-09 applied to the inline-SQL acceptance line and to the parity claim; this is the third place it is owed. The gap that was NOT acceptable to record - list_candidates, the only regression class reachable on today's corpus - was closed with a test instead.

open_findings.what: graph_snapshot calls EventRepository::list(.., version + 1), which is now a regex plus two correlated EXISTS per row where it was a LEFT JOIN
open_findings.detail: The handler fetches all events up to `version` and filters client-side (a pre-existing shape, flagged in its own comment). PR-09 makes each scanned row pay one regexp_matches over payload::text plus a primary-key probe per uuid found. For a high graph version that is a near-full scan of `events` with per-row work that the previous LEFT JOIN did not have. No measurement was taken - the throwaway test database is not a workload - so this is a note, not a claim. Measure before optimising; the obvious fix is to push the `graph_version <= $n` bound into the repo function so the filter applies to a bounded row set.

open_findings.what: viewer_route_table_lint.rs::measure_fail_open_scope_sites is a raw `src.matches(needle).count()` with NO comment stripping, so it cannot distinguish a fail-open site from a doc comment QUOTING one. PR-10 fixed both webhooks.rs sites and then re-registered one by documenting the removed idiom verbatim in delete_webhook's doc comment; the ratchet went red with 'webhooks.rs: expected 0, found 1 [REGRESSION]'.
open_findings.workaround_taken: The doc comment spells the idiom without the `axum::` path segment, and says why in place.
open_findings.why_it_matters: Every one of the eight remaining FAIL_OPEN_SCOPE_SITES rows is assigned to PR-16, and each will hit this identically the moment its fix is documented. Compare no_bypass_in_handlers.rs, which strips `//` comments for exactly this reason - the two lints in the same repo disagree about whether a comment counts.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Apply no_bypass_in_handlers.rs::strip_line_comments to the source before counting, in the PR that next lowers a row.

open_findings.what: The webhook fan-out treats 'the payload names a claim id with no `claims` row' as visible-and-deliver. routes/batch.rs::batch_create_claims exercises that branch on every request: it inserts only into AppState::claim_store and publishes a ClaimSubmitted per claim, so the claim id, submitting agent id and truth value reach every active subscription with no tenancy decision made.
open_findings.why_it_matters: hidden_claim_ids' contract ('an id that names no row at all is not returned') is right for PR-09's use - redacting rows already fetched from a viewer-scoped source - and permissive for a delivery decision to an arbitrary external URL. PR-12 will not fix it, because the row still will not exist. NOT a PR-10 regression: before PR-10 every event went to every subscriber unconditionally.
open_findings.why_not_fixed_in_pr10: Both in-scope fixes are wrong. Suppressing on named-but-absent would suppress nearly everything, because payload_uuids also collects agent, frame and workflow ids. Narrowing the scan to declared claim ids is the key allowlist PR-09 rejected verbatim. The doc now names the branch instead of asserting it away.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Either make batch_create_claims persist (it has no auth extractor either, so it needs its own PR), or stop it publishing ClaimSubmitted for rows that do not exist.
open_findings.owner: PR-12 or the PR that authenticates routes/batch.rs

open_findings.what: EpiGraphEvent::AgentSuspended carries SuspensionReason::{PolicyViolation, SecurityConcern, Administrative}, each with a `details: String` of operator-authored free text, plus suspended_by; ReputationChanged carries per-agent scores. Neither names a claim, so the payload-derived tenancy filter has nothing to act on and both are delivered to every active subscriber.
open_findings.why_it_matters: 'No claim content' is the wrong predicate - the property the fan-out needs is 'no cross-tenant content'. LATENT, NOT LIVE: grep over crates/ finds zero production publishers of either variant; every construction site is in epigraph-events' own tests and its event_type() round-trip fixture. The risk is that the first real publisher inherits the hole silently.
open_findings.why_not_fixed_in_pr10: Adding a delivery policy for a variant no code emits is policy without a requirement. The false claim in the module doc was withdrawn and the acceptance test was re-scoped so it no longer reads as blanket permission.
open_findings.suggested_fix: When a publisher is added, restrict AgentSuspended and ReputationChanged to the affected agent's own subscriptions, and add a test that a SecurityConcern's `details` does not reach an unrelated subscriber.
open_findings.owner: the PR that adds the first production publisher of either variant

open_findings.what: routes/admin.rs::system_stats takes no auth extractor and no check_scopes - only State(state) - and is registered on the `protected` router in both chains, so any authenticated principal with any scope reads the whole SystemStats aggregate, including WebhookStats { webhook_count }.
open_findings.why_it_matters: PR-10's boot hydration widens webhook_count from a per-process artefact to the cardinality of webhook_subscriptions across every tenant. A count, not content - but it is the one unfiltered path out of AppState::webhook_store, and it falsified the invariant repos/webhook.rs::list_active's doc originally rested its no-Viewer exemption on. That doc is corrected; the route is not.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Gate system_stats behind claims:admin, or drop webhook_count from SystemStats, or make it count only the caller's rows. Note admin.rs:1017 and :1137 both assert on webhook_count.

open_findings.what: delete_webhook writes through to webhook_subscriptions and then removes the entry from ONE process's AppState::webhook_store; boot hydration puts every row in every process. Revocation is therefore not effective process-wide, and a delete routed to a process that never saw the row 404s from the cache before the repo call.
open_findings.why_it_matters: Deployment-conditional: inert on the single-instance deployment this host runs, and the code makes no single-process assumption anywhere until PR-10's ledger stated one. A revoked endpoint keeps receiving HMAC-signed payloads from every other instance until it restarts.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Read-through cache with a TTL, or an event-bus delete notification. See D-PR-webhook-store-invalidation.
open_findings.owner: unassigned - the first PR requiring a multi-instance api

open_findings.what: Viewer::resolve (visibility.rs:269) returns Ok(Viewer{Scoped{group_ids: []}}) for a principal with no `agents` row, because GroupMembershipRepository::list_live_for_agent returns an empty Vec rather than an error. agent_may_receive therefore does NOT fail closed for a deleted agent - it demotes the subscription to a public-only subscriber.
open_findings.why_it_matters: Combined with the fact that migration 085's ON DELETE CASCADE removes the ROW but nothing evicts AppState::webhook_store, a running process keeps delivering public-visibility claims to a deleted agent's endpoint until it restarts. Wider than it will eventually be: with migration 062 defaulting visibility to 'public' and nothing transcribing ownership until PR-12, 'public-only' is currently close to 'everything'.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Have agent_may_receive (or Viewer::resolve itself) distinguish 'agent exists with no groups' from 'agent does not exist', and fail closed on the latter. Both branches are now named in agent_may_receive's doc so the 'fails closed' list is honest.

open_findings.what: `cargo check -p epigraph-api --no-default-features --all-targets --locked` -> EXIT=101. PRE-EXISTING: the same command at the base commit 3503911f -> EXIT=101 with 35 errors, including `missing field owner_id in initializer of state::WebhookSubscription`. No gate in the four-command set compiles cfg(all(test, not(feature="db"))), so this had never been measured.
open_findings.why_it_matters: Everything under that cfg - routes/admin.rs's field-incomplete WebhookSubscription literal, admin.rs::test_system_stats_reflects_webhook_store, and the 25 tests in routes/webhooks.rs's `#[cfg(not(feature="db"))] mod handler_tests` - is documentation, not coverage. Green CI was silence, not proof.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Either repair the cfg so it compiles and add the command to the gate, or delete the modules. Not done inside a security PR.

open_findings.what: register_webhook validates only that the URL is non-empty (and migration 085's `CHECK (btrim(url) <> '')` mirrors exactly that), so any caller with webhooks:write can register a link-local metadata address or a loopback port and have the api POST signed event payloads there.
open_findings.why_it_matters: Pre-existing and out of PR-10's ledgered scope, but PR-10 changes the blast radius: an SSRF-shaped target was a process-lifetime condition and is now a durable row that boot hydration re-arms on every deploy.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Scheme allowlist plus a private-range/link-local denylist at registration time.

open_findings.what: list_webhooks filters on sub.active; get_webhook does not. An inactive subscription would be invisible to list and readable by id.
open_findings.why_it_matters: Inert today - nothing anywhere sets active = false, so the column only ever holds its DEFAULT TRUE. It becomes a real list/get divergence, with the id-addressed route on the permissive side, the moment a deactivation path is added. Same class as the ownership divergence PR-10 fixed.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Add the active check to get_webhook in the PR that introduces deactivation.
open_findings.owner: the PR that adds a webhook deactivation path

open_findings.what: routes/community.rs::add_member takes only a ViewerExtractor and State - no scope extractor, no community-admin check, and no requirement that the perspective being added belongs to the caller. remove_member has neither a Viewer nor a scope extractor.
open_findings.why_it_matters: It routes around the declassification control PR-11 just hardened, for the whole `community` partition. access_control.rs::check_content_access's "community" arm returns ContentAccess::Full to any requester owning a perspective that is a member of the gating community, so instead of calling the now-gated update_partition, any authenticated agent creates a perspective, POSTs it into the gating community, and reads everything behind it. The two existence pre-checks are viewer-filtered, but migration 062 defaults visibility to 'public', so on today's corpus that filter excludes nothing. remove_member is the integrity twin: any authenticated agent can evict any perspective from any community.
open_findings.suggested_fix: A require_community_admin-shaped membership check plus a scope extractor, mirroring groups::add_member (which takes RequireScopeGroupsAdmin AND calls group_authz::require_group_admin).
open_findings.owner: PR-16 for the scope extractor and the admin-shaped rule; PR-12 closed the self-service grant and the self-service eviction.
open_findings.status: SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED BY PR-12, and PR-12 is why it had to be. Projecting the membership moved the hole out of check_content_access's community arm (which PR-14 deletes) and into the group_memberships / Viewer::resolve control plane, which SURVIVES PR-14 and is armed by PR-17 - i.e. it was on its way from a soon-to-be-deleted ACL bug to a durable tenancy bypass. CommunityRepository::add_member and ::remove_member now enforce CLOSED MEMBERSHIP (the acting agent must hold a live membership in the community's projected group; bootstrap exception only when that group has none, because migration 068 left every projected group with zero administrators by design; remove_member additionally always permits removing your own perspective). remove_member's handler, which previously extracted nothing at all, now takes a ViewerExtractor, and create_community passes the authenticated creator so a community created through the route is never in the bootstrap state. Gating only the PROJECTION would not have worked: 071's shim replays it out of community_members on every community-partitioned ownership write.
open_findings.residual: The rule is deliberately weaker than the suggested require_community_admin: community groups have no admins to require. A community whose group is genuinely memberless is still open to the first joiner, and no scope extractor was added. Both are PR-16's, with its viewer_route_table_lint.rs set.

open_findings.what: get_ownership (HTTP and MCP) and HTTP owned_nodes take no Viewer. OwnershipRepository::get and ::get_for_owner are not viewer-spliced, so any authenticated caller reads owner_id, partition_type and community_id for any node, and can enumerate which of an arbitrary agent's nodes are 'private'.
open_findings.why_it_matters: PR-11 gated the WRITES on this table and left the READS open. The disclosed owner_id is precisely the field the new gate's decision turns on, so the read side is a free oracle for the write gate's input. The available predicate (owner_id = viewer.principal()) is the same one the gate itself uses; the reason it was not applied is sequencing, not unavailability.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Narrow owned_nodes to the caller's own principal and 404 get_ownership for a non-owner - or delete the surface, which is what PR-14's Files line already says it does.

open_findings.what: require_declassify_authority reads the owner of record, then OwnershipRepository::assign_with_community runs INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (node_id) DO UPDATE with no `WHERE owner_id = $expected` and no enclosing transaction. ownership.node_id also carries no FK and no node-existence check.
open_findings.why_it_matters: A row created by the true owner inside the read-decide-write window is clobbered by a write the gate never authorized against; and because access_control.rs maps a missing ownership row to ContentAccess::Full, self-claiming an unowned node followed by update_partition is a two-call public->private seizure of any node id in the graph, existing or not. PR-11 narrows this relative to its predecessor (assign-to-anyone became assign-to-self-only) but does not close it. Inert on today's corpus: plan :2285 records that no write path ever inserts an ownership row (expected census 0).
open_findings.suggested_fix: An assign_if_owner / assign_if_unowned repo function whose DO UPDATE arm carries the authorized precondition, with the handler 403ing on zero rows affected. Needs the tenancy columns PR-16 adds; the seizure class is PR-18's.
open_findings.owner: PR-16 for the atomic write, PR-18 for the seizure class
open_findings.pr12_note: PR-12 changed the SEVERITY of this, in both directions. Migration 071 makes the seizure land on the LIVE tenancy columns rather than an inert ACL table, and PR-12's own arm (a)/arm (c) manufacture the seizable population (superseded private claims and all evidence carry no ownership row, so owner_of_record is None). That would have promoted it from a DoS to a confidentiality break. Migration 071's transfer guard prevents that: a declarer who is not a live member of the node's CURRENT owner_group_id cannot move it. Self-claiming an ownerless PUBLIC node still works, so the finding stands as filed.

open_findings.what: tool_viewer_coverage.rs::viewer_acquisition_lives_in_server_rs_not_in_the_tool_modules does a raw `contains("request_viewer")` over src/tools/*.rs, so a DOC COMMENT naming the helper fails the test.
open_findings.why_it_matters: It cost this PR a red shard: a doc paragraph in perspectives.rs explaining which principal the stdio transport resolves tripped it, and the fix was to reword prose rather than change any code. Same class as F-PR10-fail-open-lint-counts-comments. A lint that a comment can break trains contributors to avoid naming the thing they are documenting.
open_findings.suggested_fix: Strip comments before scanning, or match `request_viewer(` at a call position rather than the bare identifier.

open_findings.what: A harvester_fragments row inserted BEFORE its harvester_claim_provenance row is stamped by no trigger: arm (c) cannot cover the table (no claim_id) and arm (d) fires only on a claims UPDATE. It keeps ('public', world) permanently.
open_findings.status: PR-12's backfill closes it for rows existing at backfill time; new rows in that order remain a gap.
open_findings.owner: PR-13 or PR-16 — a provenance-side AFTER INSERT trigger on harvester_claim_provenance is the natural fix and needs a migration number.

open_findings.what: CommunityRepository::create now sets groups.created_by_agent_id and an admin membership WHEN A CREATOR IS KNOWN, but POST /api/v1/communities extracts no AuthContext and passes None. The communities migration 068 already projected have no creator column to derive one from either.
open_findings.owner: PR-16 for the route authentication (its viewer_route_table_lint.rs set), PR-18 for the pre-existing projected groups.

open_findings.what: tenancy_transcription_log is node_id PRIMARY KEY, so a node reclassified twice keeps only the last transition. schema_contract.rs pins the 6-column shape exactly and in order, so a sequence cannot be added without a migration number; 072-084 are allocated.
open_findings.status: Accepted and pinned by a test. Migration 080's pre-flight reads existence, not history, so the gate is unaffected.
open_findings.owner: PR-18, if it ever needs the history.

open_findings.what: Arm (d) and the 071 shim both require a maintenance-role FUNCTION OWNER, which migration 070 sets. But ScopedPool::unscoped_for_maintenance still draws from the application pool until PR-15 repoints it at MAINTENANCE_DATABASE_URL, so the backfill's DSN choice is operational rather than code-enforced.
open_findings.status: Harmless while no RLS policy is ENABLEd (PR-17). PR-15 is scheduled at week 9; the backfill runs at weeks 4-5.

open_findings.what: epigraph_definer_bypass() is pg_has_role(current_user, 'epigraph_maintenance', 'MEMBER') and CI connects as a superuser, for whom pg_has_role is true of every role. Arm (d)'s and the shim's 42501 assertions therefore CANNOT fire in the suite whatever the function owner is.
open_findings.status: Mitigated, not closed. tenancy_triggers.rs::propagation_function_is_owned_by_the_maintenance_role asserts pg_proc.proowner and the EXECUTE grant from the CATALOG, which is owner-dependent and caller-independent, and is the honest instrument. A behavioural test would pass vacuously.
open_findings.owner: PR-17, which is when a non-superuser deploy role becomes load-bearing.

closed_findings.what: `_ => ContentAccess::Full // Unknown partition -> safe default` was FAIL-OPEN and mislabeled
closed_findings.resolution: FIXED by PR-06. The arm now reads `_ => ContentAccess::Redacted` with a comment explaining the inversion. Verified in the tree during PR-07 review; the finding had been left open long after it was resolved.
